transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52m
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM); Ravi Kapoor, Sofia Martinez, Evan Liu, Janelle Park (AstralWorks)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand AstralWorks' networking posture and constraints for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood. Primary asks: private endpoints or VPC peering, region gating (EU residency), KMS integration, egress IPs, and pilot timeline. SE to run a deeper network workshop next week.

Topics covered:
- Private endpoints vs cross-account VPC peering
- Regional restrictions (EU-only data plane, replicate in us-west for DR)
- KMS and key-management options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)
- Egress, NAT, and IP allowlisting needs
- Timeline and success criteria for a pilot

Action items (as discussed on call):
- Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 notes, draft peering diagram, and pilot cost/plan.
- AstralWorks to confirm egress/NAT constraints and KMS requirements.

Questions raised:
- Will Redwood accept cross-account peering or require private endpoints?
- Can we have per-tenant RBAC and audit logs shipped to customer SIEM?
- Is there a way to limit model footprint to EU-only hardware?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we've got Liam our solutions eng and Priya from success. do you want to intro quickly, Ravi?
[00:12] Ravi: yeah hi, i'm ravi, head of platform at AstralWorks. we run several ml services, we're evaluating Redwood for inference for our customer-facing agents. main constraints are data residency (EU), and we need private networking into our VPC.
[00:28] Maya: got it. quick question — when you say private networking, are you thinking VPC peering across accounts, or private endpoints / privatelink style?
[00:36] Evan: we prefer private endpoints if possible, but our infra team likes peering for lower hop counts. also curious about cross-account routing, we have strict egress audits.
[00:46] Liam: ok, both are supported in our Private offering. there are tradeoffs: peering gives lower latency but requires route table management and sometimes transitive routing controls, privatelink/private endpoint gives more controlled access with security groups and is often easier for customers that don't want full peering.
[01:05] Sofia: and from security perspective, we need audit logs, SSO with our identity provider (SAML), and customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. is that in scope?
[01:15] Maya: yes we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and you can opt for customer-managed KMS in the Private deployment. we'll send the security pack that details HSM/KMS options.
[01:26] Ravi: perfect. region gating — we need EU-only processing for PII. does Redwood let us pin a model to a region or force requests to a regional dataplane?
[01:36] Liam: yes, we have routing policies and regional pinning. for Private deployments we can provision a dataplane in eu-west-1 and disable outbound replication to other regions. there's an ops consideration for DR, we typically recommend a read-only DR in a secondary region but that can be gated.
[01:55] Janelle: what about logging — can we stream audit logs to our SIEM, and what's the retention?
[02:03] Priya: we can stream audit logs via secure delivery to your partner SIEM, retention is configurable depending on plan; we'll include required log formats in the pack.
[02:12] Evan: network specifics — we already have strict NAT egress and an internal firewall. do you need fixed outbound IPs from Redwood side to allowlist?
[02:21] Liam: for hosted endpoints you'd need Redwood egress IPs for allowlist; for Private we sit inside your VPC so egress is your control. for privatelink we still may have control-plane callbacks but those can be proxied through customer endpoints.
[02:36] Ravi: can you clarify the control plane traffic? we want zero data plane through public internet.
[02:42] Maya: for Private deployments the data plane stays in your VPC; control plane calls (metrics, billing) can be routed over a secure tunnel or via customer-managed endpoints. we document the exact ports and FQDNs in the network checklist.
[02:56] Sofia: and for compliance, we need encryption keys to be customer-managed. do you support AWS KMS CMKs or HSMs?
[03:03] Liam: yes, AWS KMS CMK is supported; we can also integrate with external HSM solution via Bring-Your-Own-Key. we'll note integration patterns and any performance tradeoffs. sometimes HSM key ops add latency to model loads but not token generation paths typically.
[03:21] Evan: latency is a big question for us. if we do peering, what's typical P99 for small prompt (<256 tokens) runs?
[03:28] Liam: depends on workload and model size; with dedicated GPUs in the same region + peering, p99s in our benchmarks were 90-160ms for 256-token workloads on mid-sized models. we'll provide your team with model profiles and expected throughput.
[03:42] Ravi: curious about cost too — dedicated vs hosted, we want predictable throughput. do you have reserved capacity?
[03:49] Maya: yes Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and SLA. for pilot we typically propose a small Dedicated pool or Private with reserved instances for baseline. we'll include pricing.
[04:00] Janelle: onboarding timeline — if we start a pilot next week, how long to stand up Private inside our VPC?
[04:07] Priya: typical onboarding for Private with simple peering or privatelink is 2-3 weeks if networking is straightforward. more complex region gating or HSM setups take longer.
[04:16] Evan: how do you handle DNS for private endpoints? we have split-horizon for internal names.
[04:21] Liam: we support private DNS zones or you can create endpoints and map hostnames; we document the DNS entries and conditional forwarding setup in the network guide.
[04:32] Ravi: any known blockers with our setup — we're on multiple cloud accounts and use centralized transit gateway in EU.
[04:39] Liam: transit gateway topologies are common; we usually recommend either creating a dedicated peering VPC for Redwood or using privatelink to avoid complex route table propagation. we'll cover both options in the design workshop.
[04:52] Sofia: audit requirements — we need immutable audit logs and proof of access controls. can Redwood provide log signatures or tamper-evident logs?
[04:59] Maya: we provide audit logs with integrity metadata and can support pushing logs to your SIEM; for higher assurance we can discuss signed logs or pushing to an S3 bucket you control with versioning + MFA delete.
[05:12] Evan: can we run a small latency benchmark before committing? like 1000 requests to a mid-sized model in eu-west-1 with privatelink?
[05:20] Liam: yes, we can do a pilot benchmark. typical approach: you let us provision in your VPC or we set up a test endpoint, then run the synthetic load and capture p50/p95/p99. we'll need an internal test agent or we can run it from our infra with your allowlist.
[05:36] Ravi: ok good. any blockers on your side when we use JIT subnet provisioning or need to avoid certain CIDR ranges?
[05:43] Liam: avoid 10.0.0.0/8 if you already use it heavily — we can accommodate most CIDR ranges but will call out conflicts in the diagram.
[05:52] Janelle: regarding tenancy, can we pin to specific hardware — e.g., no multi-tenant GPUs?
[05:58] Maya: yes, Dedicated gives single-tenant GPU pools; Private on your VPC also isolates to your tenancy. we'll include options.
[06:08] Sofia: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between customer services and Redwood endpoints?
[06:13] Liam: yes, mTLS is available for Private endpoints. cert rotation patterns are documented.
[06:20] Ravi: ok let's talk timeline and next steps — we want the security pack and a diagram then a workshop.
[06:26] Maya: action items noted. we'll send the security and network pack after this call and propose times for the 90-min workshop.
[06:33] Priya: i'll follow up with a calendar invite and include the network template (shared: https://redwood.example.com/attachments/network-template-v1.pdf).
[06:44] Evan: i'll try to get the NAT gateway ip list and our KMS policy by end of week.
[06:50] Ravi: success criteria — 1) pilot demonstrates p99 latency under x ms, 2) secure private connectivity with no public data plane, 3) KMS-managed keys in place.
[06:59] Maya: good, we'll model the pilot to those success metrics.

[07:10] (Conversation continues with minor clarifications and some cross-talk; timestamps approximate)
[15:12] Liam: note — if AstralWorks prefers privatelink we need you to open specific endpoints and we'll supply the service name and VPC endpoint service configuration.
[22:45] Sofia: one more compliance note — we need data processing addendum and data flow diagrams for legal.
[22:52] Maya: yes legal will provide a DPA template and data flow. we'll attach with the security pack.
[30:05] Evan: small transcription note — when you said KV cache earlier it sounded like "K-V cash" in notes, just flagging.
[30:12] Liam: ha yea the transcription sometimes mangles KV cache.
[40:00] Janelle: any competitor locks or procurement blockers we should be aware of?
[40:07] Ravi: procurement will evaluate price vs lock-in; Anthropic and LocalInferenceCo were mentioned as alternatives.
[45:22] Maya: we'll include a pilot price and also an option for a short Dedicated trial to show predictability.
[50:30] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with pack and calendar invites.
[50:37] Ravi: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
